pr_without_linked.title: feat: Add `FrontendEditableAdminMixin` endpoint to plugins
pr_without_linked.body:
## Description

django CMS provides editing endpoints and frontend support for general models through `FrontendEditableAdminMixin`. Specifically, it supports editing a subset of fields only.

This PR extends this feature to plugin models which have no model admin registered for themselves, but are managed by the `PlaceholderAdmin` class. Literally, a few lines of code allow us to have partial editing endpoints for plugins. These can be used for inline editing, for example.

### This PR
* Splits the `FrontendEditableAdminMixin` into two classes, a base class (`BaseEditableAdminMixin`) which provides the endpoint, and a specific class (`FrontendEditableAdmin`) that provides the interface to the model admin.
* The `BaseEditableAdminMixin` is added to the `PlaceholderAdmin` along with the appropriate methods to 
  * retrieve the object being edited
  * find its admin instance (which is its plugin class)
* Tweaks some tricks in the existing `FrontendEditableAdminMixin`:
  * Replaces `get_plugin_name` attributes by callables (makes no difference for the template engine, but does for the plugin class)
  * When changing a plugin, the response does not trigger a page reload but just a local update of the plugin through the data bridge
  * Finally, it provides the placeholder endpoints for plugin models instead of the model admin endpoint (which does not exist for placeholders) in all template tags based on `{% render_model %}

### Usage
With this PR, partial edit can be included by replacing `{{ instance.field }}` in a plugin's template by `{% render_model instance "field" "field,other_field" %}`. Upon double-click this will open a modal with two input fields: `field` and `other_fields`.

Especially interesting is the use of `{% render_model instance "field" "field" %}` which will render the field and allow editing just itself. djangocms-text will take this to inline editing if it is active. See this short demo here on an unstyled blog title field and content fields (**not plugins**):

![inlnie-fields](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e59537bf-e5b7-48ca-a879-ac375b713806)

Any field type can be edited inline if there is an apps (such as djangocms-text) supporting it for that field type. djangocms-text supports `HTMLField` and `CharField`.

direct_issues.title: Make it possible to use multi-table (concrete) inheritance for Page and Title extensions
direct_issues.body:
I just realized that when I have multi-table inheritance for TitleExtension (I guess is the same for PageExtension) and try to publish the page django-cms fails to copy the extension instance and instead save the same instance.

The reason behind this is because `BaseExtension.copy_to_public` method (https://github.com/divio/django-cms/blob/release/3.3.x/cms/extensions/models.py#L64-L87) does not nullify pk fields of parent model(s).

I'm using Django 1.8 and DjangoCMS 3.3.

I created a workaround in my project which involves overwriting whole  `copy_to_public` method without calling `super` which is totally bad thing (If I want to upgrade the CMS in the future).

I can prepare e PR with proposed solution.

linked_issues.title: [BUG] Model PageUrl should add constraint unique_together
linked_issues.body:
## Description

Each CMS `Page` can have one `PageUrl` object per language. If there are more than that, a `MultipleObjectsReturned`-exception may be raised.


## Steps to reproduce

* Edit the page which is set as Home.
* Save the content.
* Publish that page.

The `PageUrl`-object for the home page now has two entries in the database. Reason is this 
https://github.com/django-cms/django-cms/blob/21d6a6defc5a6321bd691e43eb57c112508b952f/cms/models/pagemodel.py#L292-L296
code snippet. Here `new_path` is a functional expression containing `Concat(ConcatPair(Value('parent_slug'), ConcatPair(Value('/'), F(slug))))`. Since the resulting `path` field of the home page must be an empty string the above query can't work.

## Alternative reproduction

* Create a page with a named slug and publish as a subpage of another page. 
* Create another page with the same slug, but as child of another parent page.
* Move one of those pages so that they become siblings.

Now we get two objects of `PageUrl` with the same `language` and the same `path` entry for different pages. This in my opinion is inconsistent.

I therefore strongly recommend to add `unique_together = [['path', 'language'], ['page', 'language']]` to the `Meta`-class of the `PageUrl`-class.

In my setup I already did this. This is how I found out about the two errors reported before. Otherwise I rarely ran into the problem of hitting a `MultipleObjectsReturned`-exception, whose real cause then of course is much harder to detect.


## Do you want to help fix this issue?

* [x] Yes, I want to help fix this issue and I will join #workgroup-pr-review on [Slack](https://www.django-cms.org/slack) to confirm with the community that a PR is welcome. 
* [ ] No, I only want to report the issue.

I already patched this locally and would like to know if that proposed model change makes sense.

direct_issues.title: Deprecation Warnings
direct_issues.body:
### Summary

There are a lot of deprecation warnings when running on django 1.10, which django CMS supports. It would probably be a good idea to clean those up. 

### Expected behaviour

no deprecation warnings

### Actual behaviour

Lots of warnings. Note: since django 1.10, you have to run python with `-Wd` to see the warnings. Might be a good idea to do that when running the tests suite.

Here's a list of all the warnings:

1. "Importing from `django.core.urlresolvers` is deprecated in favor of `django.urls`".
    - This is done in several places.
2. "on_delete will be a required arg for `OneToOneField` in Django 2.0. Set it to `models.CASCADE` on models and in existing migrations if you want to maintain the current default behavior." 
    - This warning happens all over the place. 
    - To fix, every `ForeignKey` in all existing migrations need to set `on_delete=models.CASCADE` if they do not already specify `on_delete`. Then, set `on_delete=models.CASCADE` on all `ForeignKey`'s in all models, unless cascade is not the intended behavior. If the behavior should be different, new migrations will need to be created after changing  the models. 
3. "Managers from concrete parents will soon qualify as default managers. As a result, the 'objects' manager won't be created (or recreated) automatically anymore on 'cms.PageUserGroup' and 'objects' declared on 'auth.Group' will be promoted to default manager. You can declare explicitly `objects = models.Manager()` on 'PageUserGroup' to keep things the way they are or you can switch to the new behavior right away by setting `Meta.manager_inheritance_from_future` to `True`."
    - This only happens once from what I can tell, but the warning is pretty self-explanatory.

There could probably be more warnings. These are only the ones I see when I run my own test suite on my own project which uses django CMS.

Plugin restrictions need to be recalculated on every request in edit and structure mode. This is of n² complexity (n: number of plugins). 

While the plugin restrictions can be widely customized, the standard implementation respects the `CMS_PLACEHOLDER_CONF` setting allowing restrictions to depend on template and slot names.

This PR caches these restriction globally in the plugin pool for all plugins that follow the standard implementation.

Potential performance optimization for fetching Page titles
linked_issues.body:
Hi everyone, sorry for not using a template but this is not for a bug template.

I have a technical question regarding performance optimizations for CMS. I’ve noticed that retrieving titles of the pages are not optimized and I’m wondering is there a reason why it was implemented like this. Here is an example:

`[page.get_title() for page in Page.objects.filter(id__in=[1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7])]`

Creates 8 queries to the database, but if you add a prefetch_related to the query set it also does 8+1 queries (one is for retrieving all the titles for these pages):

`[page.get_title() for page in Page.objects.prefetch_related("title_set").filter(id__in=[1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7])]`

This can be optimized if we change the way the title cache is populated on the line:
https://github.com/django-cms/django-cms/blob/develop/cms/models/pagemodel.py#L1434.

Instead of doing
`titles = Title.objects.filter(page=self)`
we could do
`titles = self.title_set.all()`

And this will create only two queries, and the number of queries won’t increase linearly with the number of pages.
I’m wondering is there a reason why titles are fetched this way?

I could create a PR if DjangoCMS core contributors agree on the change.

linked_issues.title: graceful plugin exceptions
linked_issues.body:
Sometimes a plugin can cause an exception based on whatever is entered by the user, or because of other causes (e.g an api that is unreachable). Obviously this is a bug in the plugin, but it can happen and it can happen on production servers. Currently we let the exception bubble up and show a 500 page. In production this is a desaster, because with frontend editing, you can't even navigate the the page and remove the offending plugin anymore. The user is completely blocked concerning that page and has to get a developer to fix the bug before any more content can be entered on the page.

I propose that plugin rendering for each plugin has a try/except around it. To Visitors the offending plugin should just not be rendered (or an error message?). To content editors the plugin should be rendered in a way that is clear that something went wrong (perhaps with a red border and a message in the notification area at the top of the screen). In structure view the plugin should also be highlighted. In any case it should be possible to still edit or remove the plugin.
In any case the error should be logged with a traceback.

This behaviour should be controlled by a new setting that uses `DEBUG` as a default but can be overridden.

linked_issues.body: ## Description Admin UI text in Page Global Permissions has unclear meanings. [Original report.](https://django-cmsworkspace.slack.com/archives/C01EBCEK49E/p1692654745963519) ## Steps to reproduce ### "View restricted" 1. Go to '`/admin/cms/globalpagepermissions/add`. 2. Find "on page level" (fields description) > "View restricted" (checkbox label). ### "frontend view restriction" 1. Go to '`/admin/cms/globalpagepermissions/add`. 2. Find "on page level" (fields description) > "View restricted" (checkbox label). 3. Underneath it, read "frontend view restriction". ### "Edit permissions required" 1. Go to '`/admin/cms/globalpagepermissions/add`. 2. Add permission for user or group: 1. Check "Can publish". 2. Check nothing else. 4. Submit 5. See error "Users can't […] Edit permissions required." ## Expected behaviour Text that has less interpretations, and such that the correct interpretation is easy to determine. ### "View restricted" Because it actually means `not can_view` ([ref.](https://django-cmsworkspace.slack.com/archives/C01EBCEK49E/p1692688566786649?thread_ts=1692654745.963519&cid=C01EBCEK49E)), maybe something like: > Can not view restricted pages. But, what are "restricted pages"? ### "frontend view restriction" Because it actually describes `not can_view` ([ref.](https://django-cmsworkspace.slack.com/archives/C01EBCEK49E/p1692688566786649?thread_ts=1692654745.963519&cid=C01EBCEK49E)), mayeb soemthing like: > Hides restricted pages from selected user/group. But, what are "restricted pages"? But how to keep "Can edit" in sync with the label text to which it refers? ### "[…] Edit permissions required" Maybe, > Ensure user has "Can edit" permission But how to keep "Can edit" in sync with the label text to which it refers? ## Actual behaviour ### "View restricted" Label text "View restricted" is unclear because of multiple interpretations: - "View (as a verb) restricted [what]". - "View [of … what … is] restricted". ### "frontend view restriction" Help text "frontend view restriction" is unclear because of it creates more questions than it answers: - There is a restriction? - This makes a restriction? - Is the restriction active when checked or not checked? - Can I restrict a backend view from this page? ### "[…] Edit permissions required" Error text "Edit permissions required" is unclear because of multiple interpretations: - "Edit permissions [are] required." - "Edit (as a verb) [the] permissions [that are] required." ## Screenshots | View restricted | frontend view restriction | […] Edit permissions required | | - | - | - | | ![View restricted](https://github.com/django-cms/django-cms/assets/62723358/4aff7269-df28-451f-a8bf-45a1354b41f7) | ![frontend view restriction](https://github.com/django-cms/django-cms/assets/62723358/ad7c3ea7-b779-4ab9-a7f8-4bd970bf94ef) | | ## Additional information (CMS/Python/Django versions) - Django CMS: 3.8.0 - Django: 3.2 - Python: 1.4.0 ## Do you want to help fix this issue? * Yes, I want to help fix this issue and I will join #workgroup-pr-review on [Slack](https://www.django-cms.org/slack) to confirm with the community that a PR is welcome. * Maybe, and if Yes, then I agree to the above. * [x] No, I only want to report the issue.

direct_issues.title: [BUG] Special characters in page title
direct_issues.body:
## Description

If a page title contains special characters, such as `&`, then this character is rendered as HTML-entity, for instance `&`.
In browser tabs this does not look right.


## Steps to reproduce

* Create a page template where the page title is used. This usually is done by adding

```html
…
<meta>
  {% page_attribute "page_title" as page_title %}
  <title>{{ page_title}}</title>
  …
</meta>
…
```


* Create or edit a page and use `A & B` as the page title.
* Load the page.

The browser tab shows `A & B`.

## Expected behaviour

The browser tab should show `A & B` as page title.


## Do you want to help fix this issue?

By patching the templatetag `cms.templatetags.cms_tags.PageAttribute` and [not escaping the value](https://github.com/django-cms/django-cms/blob/fa7b89ceec3bd22e031be8e9cf2328a3f9434b12/cms/templatetags/cms_tags.py#L411), this can be fixed easily. However, I don't know what security implications this fix may have.

I would exempt escaping the string, whenever the name is `page_title`, just as we do it with values of type `datetime`.

Any objections to this?

pr_without_linked.title: fix: apphooks at endpoints
pr_without_linked.body:
## Description

Apphooks are available on site but currently not at the edit or preview endpoints: If they exists the page's page contents is shown/offered for editing. IMHO this might be confusing for users since those page contents are shadowed by the apphook on the public site.

This PR catches apphooks in the preview/edit views of the respective endpoints and replaces the page by the apphook's view (if existent else an error page is shown).

This should improve usability when navigating sites with apphooks in preview mode.

## Demo

Select view on an app hooked page content in the page tree gets you to the preview endpoint not triggering the app hook. **Expected behaviour: show the app hook already at the preview endpoint**.

![no-apphook](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/16904477/221154324-27b9f726-d729-480f-ab8a-6ec6d5b22160.gif)

<!--

or any other resource.

direct_issues.title: Menu cache keys are not expiring correctly
direct_issues.body:
The menu cache works by creating a unique cache key for each user, site & language combo.
If the user is not logged in, then the key is unique for site and language only.

Because these keys are created for each user, the cms stores a reference to the keys in the database under the model `CacheKey`, this allows the cms to delete all cached entries when something changes, without having to recompute the key for every user.

When a page is requested, the cms will load the menu which as a first step checks if the cache key for this user exists in the cache server, if it does then it will immediately return the result, otherwise it will discover and process all menu nodes and then store the nodes in the cache server **and** create a reference to the key used on the cache server, in the `CacheKey` model.

This pattern can lead to a case where if the cache key does not exist in the database (`CacheKey` model) but it exists in the cache server, any content that is there will be served, even though it could be outdated.

Normally, when a page is published or changed, the cms will clear the cache.
Clearing the cache involves getting all keys from the `CacheKey` model and deleting each one through django's cache api.

But there is a problem where the keys go out of sync, thus recreating the scenario mentioned above.

This problem was introduced by https://github.com/divio/django-cms/pull/1252, where cache keys in the database are cleared but their counterpart in the cache server are not.

To reproduce this, depending on the machine used, make two requests at the same time and make a third one exactly one second after the first two.

pr_without_linked.title: chore: Improve pagecontent caching in page admin (esp. page tree)
pr_without_linked.body:
## Description

Historically, django CMS has used a python cache on model level for page content objects: `page.page_content_cache`.

Since django CMS 4., this cache is filled either with user-visible objects (using the default `objects` manager) or with admin-visible objects, using the `admin_manager` manager. Since each request is, either from the user side or the admin side, this same cache can be used to hold different sets of page content objects. A side effect, however, lead to some page titles in fallback languages not to be shown in the page tree.

It turns out, however, that this was not consistently done, leading to unnecessary cache misses. 

This PR splits the caches into `page_content_cache`(traditional, user-facing) and `admin_content_cache` for the page admin, to make sure no side effects can happen.

This improves the cache hits and reduces the number of database hits for the page tree effectively removing a hidden N+1 issue. The response time should improve by 20%+ (tested with local sqlite).

direct_issues.title: Impossible to redirect to home when not using i18n_patterns
direct_issues.body:
### Summary

I have a site where I don't need international URLs, so I disabled them by not using `i18n_patterns` in `urls.py`.

Let's say I have two cms pages:

* Home (path / without language prefix)
* Foo (path /foo and also without language prefix)

In the advanced settings of Foo, I can select the entry "Home (/)" in the redirect field. After submitting the form, I get the following error: "Enter a valid URL."

The redirect field (`PageSmartLinkField`) uses `validate_url`. `validate_url` gets `value='/'` and calls `RegexValidator(regex=relative_url_regex)(value)`. I think the issue is that `relative_url_regex` does not match the path `/`. It only matches paths like e.g. `/foo`.

I suggest to modify `relative_url_regex` so that it also matches `/` and `./` since these are valid paths.


### Expected behaviour

Redirect field accepts `/`.

#### Actual behaviour

Redirect field does not accept `/`. The error "Enter a valid URL." is shown.

#### Environment

* Python version: 3.6.1
* Django version: 1.10.7
* django CMS version: 3.4.3

change method

class CMSSitemap(Sitemap):

    def lastmod(self, page_url):

        …

However, suppose we have a page which is published in both versions. We now click on the page content settings on the German version and then use the language tab on top of the form to switch the language to English.
This results in an empty form without title, slug or anything that the *already existing english version of this page* provides. If we continue to fill out the form and save it, we can create an inconsistent state inside the DB because the `PageUrl` objects now return 2 results for the english page version.

pr_without_linked.body:
## Description

A new feature added to v4 Preview and Edit endpoints. Currently there’s no way of knowing what the current pages live url is like you used to be able to with 3.x using ?edit, this new feature (off by default) adds a query string parameter to the preview and edit endpoints.

Preview endpoint: http://127.0.0.1:8000/en/admin/cms/placeholder/object/3/preview/372/
Edit endpoint: http://127.0.0.1:8000/en/admin/cms/placeholder/object/3/edit/372/
Live url: /en/blog/

Edit endpoint: http://127.0.0.1:8000/en/admin/cms/placeholder/object/3/edit/372/?live-url=/en/blog/
Live url: /en/blog/

This PR introduces two settings, CMS_ENDPOINT_LIVE_URL_QUERYSTRING_PARAM_ENABLED and CMS_ENDPOINT_LIVE_URL_QUERYSTRING_PARAM. With the former set True, and a param (as a string) provided with the latter, the preview and edit endpoints for PageContent will append the live-url as a query string parameter.

I'm not quite sure how to handle this case. Should I add more webhook activity checks inside send_webhook_request_async task or maybe catch this edge-case exception to fail gracefully? Any ideas?

Second thing: Do we want to do the sam analogically for deleting App? (deactivate webhook in app deletion)

linked_issues.body:
### What are you trying to achieve?

The `checkoutPaymentCreate` can be run during `checkoutComplete` performing, it can cause the deactivation of the payment that is currently performed in the `checkoutComplete` mutation - we should prevent such a situation.


### Steps to reproduce the problem

It can be hard to reproduce as the `checkoutPaymentCreate` mutation need to be called during `process_payment` calls in `checkoutComplete` mutation, but the steps are:
1. Create checkout
2. Update shipping method if needed
3. Run `checkoutPaymentCreate` the payment object will be created
4. Run zcheckoutComplete` mutation
5. In the meantime, when waiting for a response from the gateway, run `checkoutPaymentCreate` once again.
6. It should end up with a situation that the payment was process for inactive payment, the second uncharged payment will be active.

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/40886528/199694038-feb5c5fb-a16d-47d3-bb0e-5326badfeeee.png)


### What did you expect to happen?

Running `checkoutPaymentCreate` should be blocked when `checkoutComplete` is run.

pr_without_linked.body:
Port of https://github.com/saleor/saleor/pull/18528

- Extended `CheckoutSettingsInput` with a new `automatic_completion` field, replacing and deprecating `automatically_complete_fully_paid_checkouts`.
- `automatic_completion` input now supports:
  - `enabled` — toggles automatic checkout completion.
  - `delay` — optional delay before completion; defaults to a predefined value when omitted.

pr_without_linked.title: Fix DB locks - never-evaluated `select_for_update` querysets
pr_without_linked.body:
While working on other stuff, I found locking code where the `select_for_update` queryset was built and assigned but never evaluated. Querysets are lazy, so no SQL ran at all - no `FOR UPDATE` lock was taken and the `bulk_update` that followed ran unlocked, in arbitrary row order (deadlock risk against other writers)

- Fixed by forcing evaluation with `list(...)` inside the transaction
- Added the `assert_locks_rows_before_write` fixture, which asserts an ordered
  `FOR UPDATE` query runs before the `UPDATE` - to catch missing locks
- Documented the pitfall in `AGENTS.md`

I want to merge this change because

Before:
- `productVariantUpdate` executed with `metadata` or `privateMetadata` did not emit `ProductVariantMetadataUpdated` event
- `metadataUpdate` properly emitted this event

After
- `productVariantUpdate` now emits `ProductVariantMetadataUpdated` if metadata field was used (and actually changed).
- `ProductVariantMetadataUpdated` is not emitted if metadata was not provided or not changed in DB
- `metadataUpdate` behaves without change
